rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results <U+2014> the authors develop a model (600 random hydrant configurations of the Sinistra Ofanto on-demand district, LIDM pipe sizing, characteristic curves) and report their own laboratory tests of hydrant flow regulators (Fig. 3) and sprinkler distribution patterns (Fig. 4), plus simulation outputs (Figs. 6-10).
rows.notes: The study does not compare the investment cost of on-demand collective networks with any alternative delivery arrangement, so it offers no own result on the claim that on-demand networks cost more because supply is guaranteed at peak periods. What it shows is a cost-reliability trade-off within the on-farm sprinkler network supplied by one hydrant of an on-demand system: the design optimised for a low hydrant pressure (D24, larger pipes) is 38% more expensive than D34 but never fails across all simulated hydrant pressures, whereas cheaper small-pipe designs (D49, D55) fail with 90-100% probability at peak demand (1,200 l/s). This concerns on-farm network pipe sizing, not the on-demand distribution network itself, and the performance/failure results are simulation outputs (hydraulic model with lab-derived input curves) that are not compared with measurements from the real system. Authors themselves state results are very specific to the case study and that wind was neglected.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a methodological case study of one hydrant (789) and one ~1 ha sprinkler sector in the Capitanata district, Italy; only cost component considered is pipe cost.
